title: Compensation when Electricity Retailer Exits Market
what_it_is: Compensation when Electricity Retailer Exits Market

sections.label: Electricity retailer exit safeguards
sections.summary: The Code requires fair contracting, and EMA safeguards require exiting retailers to refund deposits and seek novation before consumers transfer to SP Group.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Electricity retailers are also licensed under the Electricity Act and regulated under the Code of Conduct for Retail Electricity Licensees, called the Code.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Code requires retailers to comply with fair contracting practices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Energy Market Authority (EMA) has implemented some safeguards in retailer exits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Exiting retailers are required to refund all security deposits collected from household consumers after offsetting outstanding charges.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Exiting retailers must also approach other retailers to seek their interest and agreement to accept the novation of the contracts on the same terms and conditions, before the consumer can be transferred to SP Group under the default supply arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Between October and December 2021, six electricity retailers exited the market.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: While the CPFTA and the Code do not require exiting retailers to compensate their consumers, three exiting retailers – Best Electricity, Ohm Energy and UGS Energy – have committed to provide ex-gratia payments or private settlements to ease their consumers' transition.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: EMA will review the current regulatory regime and will seek to strengthen the licensing and regulatory requirements for electricity retailers to better protect consumer interests.
